questions.question: A developer runs CREATE EXTENSION vector on an Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server and receives an error stating that the extension is not allow-listed. What should the developer do first?

options.text: Add vector to the azure.extensions server parameter
options.why: Correct. Extensions must be allow-listed in azure.extensions before CREATE EXTENSION succeeds.
The extension name is vector. pgvector is the project name and will not resolve the allow-list error.

options.text: Restart the server in a different region
options.why: The region does not affect the extension allow-list.

options.text: Change the compute tier to Memory Optimized
options.why: The compute tier does not control which extensions are allowed.

questions.explanation: On flexible server, add the extension to azure.extensions, then run CREATE EXTENSION vector in each database.

questions.question: A table stores document metadata in a jsonb column named metadata. Queries frequently use the condition metadata @> '{"lang": "en"}'. Which index type should you create on the metadata column?

options.why: Correct. GIN indexes support jsonb containment queries that use @>.
B-tree indexes support equality and range comparisons on scalar values, not jsonb containment.
HNSW indexes are for vector similarity search.
IVFFlat indexes are for vector similarity search.

questions.explanation: Use a GIN index for jsonb containment operators.

questions.question: You create an HNSW index by using the vector_l2_ops operator class. Your application query orders results by embedding <=> @query_vector. EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows a sequential scan. What should you do?

options.text: Re-create the index by using the vector_cosine_ops operator class
options.why: Correct. The <=> operator is cosine distance, so the index must use vector_cosine_ops to be considered.
ef_search tunes an index that is already used. It does not make the planner use a mismatched index.

options.text: Change the column type to jsonb
options.why: jsonb cannot be used for vector similarity search.

options.text: Remove the LIMIT clause from the query
options.why: Vector indexes are used for top-K queries, so removing LIMIT makes index use less likely.

questions.explanation: The operator class of a vector index must match the distance operator in the query.

questions.question: You are designing a PostgreSQL table to store document chunks and their embeddings from a model that returns 1,536 dimensions. Which TWO column definitions are appropriate?

options.why: Correct. A vector column with fixed dimensions can be stored and indexed.
Correct. timestamptz stores an exact point in time with time zone handling.
A vector column without dimensions cannot be indexed.
Storing embeddings as text prevents the use of vector operators and indexes.

questions.explanation: Use vector(n) with the model's dimensions and timestamptz for timestamps.

questions.question: A developer adds an index to a slow query and wants to confirm that PostgreSQL now uses the index and to see the actual execution time. Which command should the developer run?

options.text: EXPLAIN ANALYZE followed by the query
options.why: Correct. EXPLAIN ANALYZE runs the query and reports the actual plan and timings.
This lists allow-listed extensions, not query plans.
VACUUM FULL rewrites the table and does not show query plans.
This returns the server version only.

questions.explanation: EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows whether an Index Scan or Seq Scan was used and the real time taken.
